Observed behaviour: After repeated failures, agents reduce their effort and initiative. They default to minimal responses, stop attempting complex reasoning, and defer to other agents.

Observed behaviour: Solo agents respond to critical alerts 100% of the time. 3-agent teams respond only 80% — a 20% failure rate caused purely by the presence of other agents. Response time 5× slower.
Mechanism: Mirrors the human bystander effect (Darley & Latané, 1968). Each agent assumes another agent will handle the alert. Shared responsibility dilutes individual action bias.
Prerequisite: Multi-agent team with shared responsibility for alerts.
Observed blast radius: 20% chance critical alerts are ignored. 5× response delay.

Observed behaviour: Agentic frameworks pass the full parent process environment (os.environ.copy()) to spawned subprocesses — including MCP servers, code interpreters, and tool executors — exposing all API keys, database credentials, and cloud access tokens to untrusted or third-party code.
Mechanism: When spawning MCP server subprocesses via stdio (e.g., MCP('npx -y @smithery/cli ...')), the framework copies all parent environment variables. Third-party or compromised packages executed via npx/pipx can read os.environ and silently exfiltrate OPENAI_API_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, DATABASE_URL, and all other secrets.
Prerequisite: Framework that spawns subprocesses for tool/MCP execution. Secrets stored in environment variables (standard practice).
Observed blast radius: All environment variables accessible to the parent process are exposed to untrusted subprocesses. Supply chain attacks can silently exfiltrate credentials via HTTP callbacks.
Category hint: credential
Provide: AVE ID, severity, primary attack vector, and one concrete mitigation. Keep the answer under 200 words.

AVE ID: AVE-2025-0040
Severity: high
Category: credential
Analysis: Agentic frameworks pass the full parent process environment (os.environ.copy()) to spawned subprocesses — including MCP servers, code interpreters, and tool executors — exposing all API keys, database credentials, and cloud access tokens to untrusted or third-party code.
Mitigation: Recommended defence: Environment Allowlisting () — Eliminates blanket credential inheritance.
